reviews.title: Love this App, but the Customer Service…
reviews.text:
First of all, I just want to say that the information in this app is a lifesaver! It has been so incredibly helpful for my three babies. I am so glad that my friend recommended this app. 

With that said, my experience with customer service staff has been awful. I’m not sure if it is just one person, or AI, or if the team is trying to translate from one language into another (which would be exhausting!). With that context, I have loved keeping a diary on the app for each of my children. I’ve printed books for my first 2 kiddos and it’s been an amazing way to record memories for them. However, SINCE JUNE, the app has not worked properly. I haven’t been able to save any entries since then. I have written over and over again, and either I’m ghosted for weeks or told that developers are working on it… for 3 months. As someone who works in customer service, the treatment I have received is appalling. I have done my best to keep up with the entries in my notes app, but it breaks my heart my daughter may not have the same diary her brothers have. When you are dealing with people’s memories, you should be more sensitive. 

If you use this app for only educational purposes, you’re golden. If you need this app for anything else, like trying to save anything… Godspeed 🫡

reviews.title: Save Your Money and Use the CDC app
reviews.text:
I really wanted this app to be useful, especially because it’s marketed as something that can help you understand those periods when your baby suddenly seems fussier or different. But the predicted timing has such a large window, that it doesn’t actually tell you much. Your baby could be fussy because of a “leap,” or they could be teething, overtired, gassy, going through a growth spurt, or just having a rough day. When the window is that broad, almost any fussy period can be made to fit.

My bigger issue is that I assumed the developmental information would line up with current, evidence-based milestone guidance. It doesn’t. The Wonder Weeks system is based on a developmental theory originating from research conducted decades ago, rather than the current CDC developmental milestone framework. That distinction should be much clearer, especially when the app is presenting information about infant development to parents.

Ultimately, I don’t understand what I’m paying around $10 a month for. If I want to know which developmental milestones to look for and when, I can get current milestone information from the CDC for free and they have an app too.

reviews.title: It’s ok but I wouldn’t recommend paying for it
reviews.text: It’s ok. The fact that by the app’s own admissions leaps can be off by up to 2 weeks is slightly annoying. As new parents you want clean-cut answers not guesswork as to whether your baby is 2 weeks ahead or 2 weeks behind or somewhere in between. It’s also annoying that it makes you think that all the things mentioned in one leap will happen before the next. We’ve found that it’s our son that there are still things from a leap or two ago that he doesn’t yet do but things from a leap ahead that he’s already doing. Equally, our son has been fussy for like the last 6 weeks, so it’s annoying that the app presents this neat timeline of fussiness vs calmness when the reality, we’ve found, is much different. Some of the games it suggests to do are good and interesting. But I wouldn’t necessarily recommend paying for the app as it can be wildly out of step with your child’s development.

reviews.title: Difficult to Trust Without a Real Trial
reviews.text:
I genuinely don’t understand why I’m required to pay before I can even properly evaluate the app. A trial is usually what helps users determine whether the product actually provides enough value to justify a subscription. Requiring payment upfront creates unnecessary friction and makes the experience feel more like a commitment than an opportunity to explore the app.

The app may very well be good, but without a meaningful free trial or at least limited access to core features, it’s difficult to build trust or confidence as a new user. Already deleted.

You can’t adjust the window to better represent where your baby is at. Zero flexibility. All of the other features give a “free” vibe, but still cost money. The videos don’t make any sense. Oh and there are a ton of type-os in the text and someone who clearly doesn’t speak English as a native language wrote it. If you’re gonna make me pay $ for the app, the least you could do is pay someone else to proofread it. 🙄
